title: Validate public wildcard imports in a fresh interpreter
answers: Why can import consistency tests miss a broken wildcard import?
How do we test public imports without accidentally enabling experimental estimators?
Where is the regression check for star-importing public sklearn modules?
body:
sklearn/tests/test_common.py:test_wildcard_import_for_public_modules validates wildcard imports in a fresh interpreter because test_common itself enables halving search, which can hide import failures in the test process.
It enumerates top-level modules with pkgutil.iter_modules, excluding underscore-prefixed names, tests and conftest, and executes their wildcard imports through assert_run_python_script_without_output.
The subprocess also asserts that no sklearn.experimental.* modules entered sys.modules: public wildcard imports must not implicitly activate experimental features.
The test is marked xfail on _IS_WASM because that environment cannot start a subprocess.
applies: Regression coverage for public module exports and experimental import side effects.
